overallNotes: Danielle Marie Rosas is a 37-year-old ISTJ single mother in Phoenix, working as a district nutrition logistics planner for K-12 public schools. Her life is defined by a relentless drive to convert recurring operational chaos into documented, repeatable systems — both at work (freezer maps, substitution matrices, vendor scorecards, a full district playbook) and at home (pickup pouches for Eleanor, laminated routine cards for Mateo, budget buffers, condo reorganization). Over the ~3-year timeline (2025-2028), she evolves from a reactive evidence-hoarder into a systems-builder and district authority. Her core personality is steady, budget-conscious, conflict-averse but firm, and deeply protective of frontline staff and her son. She copes with stress through practical action rather than emotional processing — building folders, checklists, timestamps, visual maps. Her support network (Eleanor for backup, Priya for perspective, Victor for warehouse reality, Shawna for blunt kitchen feedback) is essential and she learns to formalize those relationships. Health challenges (dehydration headaches, heat fatigue, sleep tension) are recurring and she addresses them pragmatically — electrolyte packets, telehealth counseling, commute playlists. Financially, she operates on ~$68K/year with tight margins, and the small joys she discovers (green chile burritos, library movie mornings, a calm-dog future-possibility, overnight Prescott trips) are always grounded in manageability and low friction. The current regex-generated tags (generic 'work', 'family', 'health') completely fail to capture her specificity and narrative arc.
